Markdown vs. CommonMark: Understanding the Difference Markdown and CommonMark are both lightweight markup languages, but there are slight differences between the two. Markdown, created by John Gruber in 2004, was the first of its kind. It has since become widely adopted and is supported by various platforms and applications. CommonMark, on the other hand, is a standardized version of Markdown, developed to address ambiguities and inconsistencies in the original syntax. Key Features of Markdown and CommonMark 1. Simplicity and Readability One of the primary advantages of lightweight markdown languages is their simplicity. The syntax is intuitive and easy to grasp, making it accessible to both beginners and experts. Versatility and Portability Markdown and CommonMark can be used across multiple platforms, making them highly versatile. Whether you're writing on a desktop, mobile device, or even within a text editor, these languages are universally supported. This portability allows you to seamlessly transition between different environments without compromising the formatting of your content. 3. Extensibility While the syntax for Markdown and CommonMark is straightforward, both languages provide the ability to extend their functionality.
